intro.caption: Lesson 6-15 — simplifying algebraic expressions. It's swap meet day at the academy. Ozzie needs gears and springs, and Vale is selling. Three gates and a boss trade stand between the cadets and a fair deal.

balloons.t: I need gears and springs. Today, we trade.
3 gears plus 4 springs: 3g + 4s. That's 7gs. Seven gear-springs!
Seven gear-springs? I don't know what that is. That's classified. I'll take it!

pages.caption: A gear-spring is not a thing. Gears and springs are unlike terms. Only like terms — the same variable — can be combined.

balloons.t: Gears with gears. Springs with springs. Sort first.
My list says 4g + 3 + 2g. Gears, a number, more gears.
Gears go together. The 3 has no letter. It stays on its own.
Test it with numbers. Vale's math smells funny.
Last chance. Three deals. Sign them or walk away.
We read every deal first. Every term.
6g + 6s. Real gears. Real springs. Zero gear-springs.

win.caption: Like terms have the same variable. To simplify, add or subtract their coefficients and keep the variable. Numbers with no variable combine with each other. Unlike terms, like 3g and 4s, stay apart.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Sort the Parts
gates.prompt: Ivy is sorting the parts. g stands for gears and s stands for springs.
hints: Conceptual: like terms have exactly the same variable. The number in front, the coefficient, can be different.
Procedural: cover the coefficient with your finger. If the letters left over match, the terms are like terms. A lone g means 1g.

steps: 4b and b both have the variable b, so they are like terms. b means 1b.
2c has a different variable. It has no like term here.

items.q: Which of these are the same kind of part as 5g? Pick all that apply.

options.fb: Yes: same variable, g.
Same coefficient, but a different variable. Springs are not gears.
Yes: g is 1g. Same variable.
5 has no variable. It is a constant, not a gear term.
Yes: same variable, g.

items.fbMiss: You missed a gear term. Any term with just g is a like term, even g by itself.
items.fbExtra: One pick is not a gear term. Check the variable: it must be g.

items.q: Which expression has no like terms to combine?

options.fb: 3g and 4g are both gears. They combine to 7g.
2s and s are like terms. They combine to 3s.
6 and 1 are both constants, so they are like terms. They combine to 7.

gates.pass: Gears in one bin, springs in the other. 3g + 4s has nothing to combine — that's the problem with Vale's deal.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Count the Gears
gates.prompt: Ozzie's trade list says 4g + 3 + 2g. Simplify it.
hints: Conceptual: combining like terms is counting the same kind of thing. 4 gears and 2 more gears is 6 gears.
Procedural: add or subtract the coefficients of like terms and keep the variable the same. Constants combine only with constants.

steps: 5b and 3b are like terms: 5 + 3 = 8, so 8b. The 2 has no variable.

options.fb: The 3 has no g, so it cannot join the gears. Only 4g and 2g combine.
You multiplied 4 × 2. Combining like terms ADDS the coefficients: 4 + 2 = 6.
The 3 does not disappear. It stays as its own term.

items.label: 7s − 3s + s = ? s. The coefficient is
items.aria: coefficient of s after simplifying 7s minus 3s plus s

fb.msg: That's 7 − 3. The last s counts too: s means 1s.
That's 7 + 3 + 1. The 3s is subtracted, not added.
That's 7 − 3 − 1. The last s is added: + s.

items.fbDefault: Work left to right with the coefficients: 7 − 3 + 1.

gates.pass: 6g + 3 and 5s. Ozzie counts his gears twice. Same answer both times.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Fix the Claim
gates.badge: Claim Fixer — Unlike Terms Stay Apart
gates.prompt: Vale claims 3g + 4s = 7gs. Fix the claim, then test it with numbers.
hints: Conceptual: 3g and 4s have different variables, so they are unlike terms. They cannot be combined into one term.
Procedural: put numbers in for g and s. Find the value of each expression. If the values differ, the expressions are not equal.

steps: Practice: someone says 2a + 3b = 5ab. Test a = 1 and b = 4.
14 is not 20, so the claim is false. 2a + 3b is already simplified.
worked.q: Test 5m + 2n and 7mn with m = 2 and n = 3.
worked.a: 16 and 42, so they are not equal

options.fb: That's Vale's claim. g and s are different variables, so 3g and 4s are unlike terms.
That turns the 4 springs into gears. A spring is not a gear.
That multiplies the terms. Plus means add, and unlike terms cannot be added into one.

items.label: Let g = 2 and s = 5. The value of 3g + 4s is
items.aria: value of 3g plus 4s when g is 2 and s is 5

fb.msg: 35 is 7 × 5. You combined unlike terms first. Find 3 × 2 and 4 × 5 separately.

gates.pass: 3g + 4s = 26 but 7gs = 70. Vale's claim is busted. Teo un-buys his seven gear-springs.

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Final Trade
gates.prompt: Vale's last three deals. Simplify each one before anyone signs.
hints: Conceptual: combine only like terms. A lone variable has coefficient 1, and parentheses get distributed first.
Procedural: distribute if there are parentheses. Then group like terms and add or subtract their coefficients.

options.fb: The lone s counts: s means 1s, so 5s + s = 6s.
That mashes gears and springs into one term. Combine gears with gears and springs with springs.
You multiplied 2 × 4. Add the coefficients: 2 + 4 = 6. And 5s + s = 6s.
You distributed to the first term only. 3 × 2 = 6.
The 6 has no g, so it cannot join the gears.
That is equal, but not simplified. 3g and g are like terms: 3g + g = 4g.

items.label: Deal 3 · Simplify 6g + 2s − g, then find its value when g = 5 and s = 2:
items.aria: value of 6g plus 2s minus g when g is 5 and s is 2

fb.msg: You left out the − g. 6g − g = 5g, so it is 5 × 5 + 2 × 2.
− g takes away one whole g, which is 5 here, not 1.
That treats it as 8gs. Simplify to 5g + 2s first, then put in the numbers.

gates.pass: 6g + 6s, 4g + 6, and a value of 29. Every deal is fair. Vale packs up her gear-springs and leaves.

journal.heading: Lesson 6-15 — what the swap meet taught us
rows: Like terms have the same variable, like 5g, 2g and g. A lone g means 1g. Constants like 3 and 1 are like terms too.
Add or subtract the coefficients and keep the variable: 4g + 3 + 2g = 6g + 3.
3g and 4s have different variables. They stay apart: 3g + 4s is already simplified.
3g + 4s is not 7gs. Test g = 2, s = 5: 3g + 4s = 26, but 7gs = 70.
journal.quote: "I have traded gears. I have traded springs. I will never trade a gear-spring." — Chip

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 6-15 (Simplify Algebraic Expressions) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: identifying like terms and constants, combining coefficients, keeping unlike terms apart, distributing before combining, and testing values to show 3g + 4s is not 7gs.
standards: Apply the properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions
